chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who visits his brother in the outskirts of the city seeking the Face of Allah, so he is visiting Him, and it is a right upon Allah that He honours His visitor.'

key_terms.حَقٌّ عَلَى اللَّهِ: A right upon God (obligation due to His generosity)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a brother with the intention of seeking God's face?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the profound spiritual status of ziyaarah (visitation) when performed with pure sincerity (ibtigha'a wajh Allah). The phrase 'God is obligated to honor his visitor' reflects the Shia concept of God's self-binding promise (al-wajb 'ala Allah) to reward those who seek His pleasure through social bonds, elevating a simple social visit into an act of worship.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who visits his brother in the outskirts of the city seeking the Face of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he is visiting Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and would have a right upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> Honours His<sup>azwj</sup> visitor’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Whoever visits his brother (in belief) in a side of the city just to please Allah, has visited Him, and it becomes a responsibility for Allah to honor His visitor.’”
